The average sum of the concentration of all the cations in serum is 
about 150 mEq/L. The cation concentration is balanced by 150 mEq/L 
of anions, yielding a total serum osmolality of about 300 mOsm/L. An 
osmolar imbalance is caused by a gain or loss of water relative to 
a solute. An osmolality of less than 285 mOsm/L generally indicates 
a water excess; an osmolality of greater than 300 mOsm/L indicates a 
water deficit.
Water Intoxication
Water intoxication occurs as a result of water intake in excess 
of the body’s ability to excrete water. The increased intracellu-
lar fluid volume is accompanied by osmolar dilution. The 
increased volume of intracellular fluid causes the cells, particu-
larly the brain cells, to swell, leading to headache, nausea, vom-
iting, muscle twitching, blindness, and convulsions with im-
pending stupor. If left untreated, water intoxication can 
be fatal. Water intoxication is not commonly seen in normal, 
healthy individuals. It may be seen in endurance athletes 
who consume large amounts of electrolyte-free beverages
